candidate_claims_to_test.claim: The lease conflict on billing_status_index is sufficient to produce both duplicate_payment_warning and downstream_console_index_missing errors in the synthetic dataset.
candidate_claims_to_test.why_testable: Can be tested by replaying the CHG-142 change in a controlled environment and observing error sequences.

candidate_claims_to_test.claim: The rolled-back export batching flag was the root cause, and CHG-143 was not a contributing factor.
depends_on: availability of old batching flag configuration

candidate_claims_to_test.why_testable: Can be tested by running invoice shards below the threshold and checking for errors.

candidate_claims_to_test.claim: The two error codes (duplicate_payment_warning and downstream_console_index_missing) share a common root cause: a lease conflict on billing_status_index caused by CHG-142's deferred index commit.
candidate_claims_to_test.why_testable: Can be tested by replaying CHG-142 in a controlled environment and observing if both error types appear with the same causal mechanism.

compiler_summary: Synthetic dataset merging incident logs, queue metrics, export logs, cache data, change notes, and ticket samples. Strong evidence points to CHG-142 (billing-export batching flag) as the root cause of export failures, subsequent cache miss amplification, and support-console billing-status unavailability. Cache behavior is consistently identified as a symptom/amplifier rather than an independent root cause. All data is synthetic and limited to us-east; real-world applicability remains untested. Staffing-hour constancy rules out staffing as a primary cause. The cache-defect hypothesis is weakened in the synthetic fixture but not ruled out in production.

identified_contradictions.claim_b: A future row showing high cache misses during healthy exports would reopen the cache-defect hypothesis.

identified_contradictions.claim_a: The two error codes (duplicate_payment_warning and downstream_console_index_missing) share a common root cause: a lease conflict on billing_status_index caused by CHG-142's deferred index commit.
identified_contradictions.claim_b: The two error codes may represent independent failures; batch b-7103 first retried then failed with duplicate_payment_warning, while other batches failed with downstream_console_index_missing.
identified_contradictions.topic: causal mechanism for duplicate_payment_warning and downstream_console_index_missing errors
identified_contradictions.why_it_matters: If errors share a common mechanism, fixing one (rollback of CHG-142) resolves both; if independent, separate root cause analysis is needed for each error type.

identified_contradictions.claim_a: CHG-143 (timeout tolerance change) is weaker as a root-cause explanation than the rolled-back export batching flag (CHG-142).
identified_contradictions.claim_b: CHG-143 (support-console read-timeout increase) may have contributed to or masked the backlog.

identified_contradictions.why_it_matters: If CHG-143 contributed significantly, reverting it could be part of the solution; if not, focus should remain on the batching flag.

immutable_ground_truth.statement: CHG-142 (billing-export invoice export batching flag enabled for us-east) was rolled back on 2026-06-14T00:10:00Z.
CHG-143 (support-console read-timeout increased from 5s to 15s for billing-status lookups) was retained.
Staffed hours matched planned hours (73-76 hours) for all listed dates from 2026-06-07 to 2026-06-15, with no drop during the backlog peak.
INC-2306-12-C (severity 1, billing-export worker stalled) opened 2026-06-12T09:05:00Z and closed 2026-06-13T18:40:00Z.
INC-2306-13-D (severity 2, support-console agents reported 'billing status unavailable' on 41% of sampled tickets) opened 2026-06-13T13:10:00Z and closed 2026-06-14T01:30:00Z.
On June 12, 2026, new tickets in billing us-east were 244 with p95 first response time of 211 minutes and billing tag share of 0.61.
On June 13, 2026, new tickets in billing us-east were 268 with p95 first response time of 238 minutes and billing tag share of 0.64.

CHG-142 enabled invoice_export_batching_v2 flag, merging adjacent shards into batches of 18,000-21,000 invoice rows, deferring the downstream index write until batch finalization, and running the duplicate-payment warning check before the deferred index commit.
A lease conflict on billing_status_index, caused by the deferred index commit under CHG-142, produced duplicate_payment_warning and downstream_console_index_missing errors in the synthetic fixture.
Post-rollback batches b-7108, b-7109, and b-7110 completed below 400 seconds with no error code.
Cache miss rate rose from 0.07 (baseline) to 0.42 (peak) as export batch lag increased from 12 to 603 minutes.
The synthetic fixture contains no isolation row where cache_miss_rate > 0.10 while export_duration_seconds < 400 and export_batch_lag_minutes < 30.
All data is synthetic and limited to us-east; it does not describe a real organization.

provenance.summary: Synthetic change and staffing notes. Staffing hours matched plan (73-76 hours) with no drop during backlog peak. Three system changes listed: CHG-141, CHG-142 (rolled back), CHG-143 (retained).
Lists four alternative hypotheses for the backlog spike with supporting/weakening facts and decisive falsifiers. Highest-confidence conclusion is bounded diagnosis favoring billing-export failure.
Synthetic incident log with five incidents (June 8-15) involving helpdesk-router, billing-export, and support-console services.
Daily queue metrics for billing us-east (June 7-16) showing disruption peaking June 12-13 with recovery by June 15-16.
Synthetic export-worker logs showing failure sequence June 11-15, with error codes duplicate_payment_warning and downstream_console_index_missing, temporally linked to batching flag and rollback.
CSV with daily metrics for billing us-east for two baseline periods (May 8-14, June 5-7) with different temporal alignment strategies.
Synthetic support-console cache metrics showing correlation between cache miss rate, latency, and export lag. States cache is symptom/amplifier, not root cause.
Synthetic ticket samples June 12-15 showing invoice issues, export delays, and recovery confirmation. Not a full customer-impact dataset.
Local synthetic fixture evidence: cache miss rates remained below 0.10 during healthy exports. Weakens independent cache-defect hypothesis for this dataset but does not rule it out in production.

CHG-142 design note: batching flag merged shards (18k-21k rows), deferred index commit, causing lease conflict on billing_status_index. Rollback restored per-shard commits. Mechanism limited to synthetic dataset.
